implementation.name: SAP BTP ABAP Environment
implementation.version_scope: ABAP Cloud console-class workflow; account and service release specific.

fit.text: Build application classes inside a connected SAP ABAP environment; the example is not an independent desktop executable.

prerequisites.text: An ABAP environment user and Eclipse with ABAP Development Tools are required.

execution.text: Activate a class implementing IF_OO_ADT_CLASSRUN, then run it in the ADT application console.

behavior.text: Classes implement interfaces and methods; out->write sends data to the console.

tooling.text: ADT supplies project connection, package creation, class activation and console execution.

maintenance.text: Packages and transport requests belong to the connected SAP system; retain that context when moving a class.

costs.text: SAP documents licensed and trial account paths; trial setup does not establish production pricing.

example.code:
CLASS zcl_plldn DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_oo_adt_classrun.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS zcl_plldn IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_oo_adt_classrun~main.
    out->write( 'PLLDN' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
example.run_instructions: Create ZCL_PLLDN in an ADT ABAP Cloud project, paste the class, save and activate. Choose Run As > ABAP Application (Console).

licenses.notice: The setup distinguishes licensed and trial access; it does not establish a redistributable SPDX software licence.

implementation.name: Android SDK AIDL Java Binder backend
implementation.version_scope: Android application IPC workflow; not all hardware-interface backends.

fit.text: Describe cross-application Android service interfaces; ordinary local calls can use Binder directly instead.

prerequisites.text: Understand bound services and Java-style signatures before implementing the generated Stub.

execution.text: An Android app build generates Binder bindings from .aidl files; a service and client must still implement the exchange.

behavior.text: Remote calls can arrive concurrently on Binder threads; validate incoming data and synchronize shared state.

tooling.text: Android Studio or Gradle generates bindings; app code supplies onBind and ServiceConnection logic.

maintenance.text: Preserve released interface compatibility because separately installed clients carry their own definitions.

costs.text: Compiler and Android platform licences are component-specific; the AOSP policy alone is not a binary licence audit.

example.run_instructions: Place IAdder.aidl at src/main/aidl/com/example/IAdder.aidl in the documented project layout. Place the file in an Android project's AIDL source directory and build the configured project with Gradle. A bound service must extend IAdder.Stub and implement add before clients can call it.
example.expected_result: The build generates IAdder bindings. The interface alone performs no addition.

implementation.name: Dyalog APL
implementation.version_scope: Dyalog interactive array notation; licensing is Dyalog-specific.

sources.label: Dyalog array notation and execution model

fit.text: Express array transformations and numerical models interactively; the symbolic notation needs its own learning step.

prerequisites.text: Learn array expressions and APL symbol entry through the linked novice lessons or TryAPL.

execution.text: Evaluate expressions over vectors and matrices directly in the Dyalog session.

behavior.text: Reduction (+/) computes a sum; tally (≢) counts elements, so a mean needs no explicit loop.

tooling.text: Dyalog links manuals, fonts and keyboard resources; TryAPL supports simple expressions online.

maintenance.text: Multi-user deployment and distributing Dyalog with an application can require separate runtime licensing.

costs.text: Basic licensing restricts commercial purposes; Commercial development and runtime distribution have separate terms.

example.run_instructions: Enter both expressions in Dyalog or TryAPL and evaluate the final line.

licenses.scope: Dyalog development environment: proprietary Basic, Commercial and runtime agreements.
licenses.notice: Choose the agreement matching your purpose; a development licence does not itself grant all runtime distribution rights.

implementation.name: ATS2 / Postiats
implementation.version_scope: ATS2 native workflow; ATS1 and optional collectors require separate consideration.

fit.text: Combine systems programming with type-level proofs; dependent and linear types extend the learning work beyond syntax.

prerequisites.text: Study static types and resource-sensitive programming before using the proof and linear-type features.

execution.text: ATS2 generates code for a C toolchain; Postiats supplies the compiler and supporting libraries.

behavior.text: The functional core is call-by-value; linear types track resources that cannot be duplicated freely.

tooling.text: Postiats documents its compiler bootstrap and C compiler build requirements in the source distribution.

maintenance.text: Rebuilding from source involves the documented bootstrap compiler and selected optional dependencies.

costs.text: The compiler's source header permits GPL-3.0-or-later; standard-library and generated-application terms must be considered separately.

example.run_instructions: With ATS2/Postiats installed and its environment configured, compile using patscc -o hello hello.dats, then run hello.

licenses.scope: Core implementation covered by the cited source-header grant; separately marked libraries and dependencies are excluded.
licenses.notice: The compiler header expressly permits GPL version 3 or later; preserve covered-source licences and notices.

implementation.name: Apache Royale compiler and Express framework
implementation.version_scope: Royale ActionScript 3 in an MXML browser application; not legacy Flash Player.

sources.label: Royale build and run a browser application

fit.text: Build browser frontends through Royale, combining ActionScript behavior with MXML view declarations.

prerequisites.text: Install the Royale SDK; learn ActionScript data declarations and the MXML component namespaces.

execution.text: mxmlc generates browser output; open bin/js-release/index.html after successful compilation.

behavior.text: ActionScript values provide data while MXML connects the view components and properties.

tooling.text: The SDK supplies a compiler and examples; documentation links formatter, linter and testing guidance.

maintenance.text: Keep the selected SDK and framework with the project so its component namespaces resolve consistently.

costs.text: The compiler has Apache-2.0 terms; framework and bundled dependency notices must be checked separately.

example.code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<js:Application xmlns:fx="http://ns.adobe.com/mxml/2009" xmlns:js="library://ns.apache.org/royale/express">
  <fx:Script><![CDATA[
    public const greeting:String = "PLLDN";
  ]]></fx:Script>
  <js:initialView><js:View><js:Label text="{greeting}"/></js:View></js:initialView>
</js:Application>
example.run_instructions: Place HelloWorld.mxml at src/HelloWorld.mxml in the documented project layout. Run the installed Royale mxmlc src/HelloWorld.mxml from the project directory. Open the generated bin/js-release/index.html.
example.expected_result: The browser view displays a label reading PLLDN.

implementation.name: GCC GNAT native Ada compiler
implementation.version_scope: GNAT console workflow using Ada.Text_IO; target runtimes and proof tooling are separate.

fit.text: Write native programs with declared types, packages and explicit control flow; compilation alone is not a formal proof.

prerequisites.text: Install GNAT for a matching native target before compiling the console example.

execution.text: gnatmake compiles, binds and links a main procedure into an executable.

behavior.text: Declarations and package interfaces organize code; runtime checks complement static type checking.

tooling.text: The GNAT guide explains the compiler, binder and linker stages behind gnatmake.

maintenance.text: Match source filenames to their library unit names so GNAT can locate dependent units.

costs.text: GNAT compiler source has GPL-3.0-or-later terms; the cited Ada.Text_IO runtime header additionally grants GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1.

example.run_instructions: Run gnatmake hello.adb, then run hello (hello.exe on Windows).

licenses.scope: GNAT compiler components covered by the cited driver grant; runtime libraries and separately marked dependencies are excluded.
licenses.notice: The compiler header expressly permits GPL version 3 or later; preserve covered-source licences and notices.

licenses.scope: The portions covered by the cited runtime header, not all libraries.
licenses.notice: The header expressly grants the GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1.

implementation.name: Agda 2
implementation.version_scope: Dependent-type checker; built-in language constructs without external libraries.

sources.label: Agda types and proof assistant overview

fit.text: Model properties in types and develop constructive proofs; specifications also have to be written.

prerequisites.text: Learn algebraic data types and signatures before attempting dependent proofs.

execution.text: Use interactive checking or agda on a file; executable compilation is a separate backend workflow.

behavior.text: Dependent types encode value-indexed constraints; unsafe options and postulates change what is established.

tooling.text: Emacs Agda mode loads definitions and reports type errors; the documented GHC backend supports compilation.

maintenance.text: Built-in modules provide minimal support; additional standard-library bindings are separately selected dependencies.

costs.text: Agda has MIT terms; preserve copyright and permission notices when redistributing its implementation.

example.code:
module Flag where

data Flag : Set where
  ready : Flag

default : Flag
default = ready
example.run_instructions: Load Flag.agda in Emacs Agda mode with C-c C-l, or run agda Flag.agda.
example.expected_result: The checker accepts Flag and default; this example has no console output.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

implementation.name: Aiken compiler and test runner
implementation.version_scope: Documented project and unit-test workflow for Cardano validators; no network deployment.

fit.text: Develop Cardano validator logic and test component functions; a unit test does not submit a transaction.

prerequisites.text: Understand datum, redeemer and transaction context when progressing from pure functions to validators.

execution.text: aiken check compiles project modules and runs tests; on-chain deployment is a separate step.

behavior.text: Tests return Boolean results; ledger validation and test placeholders have different roles.

tooling.text: The workflow supplies dependency resolution, test traces and execution-unit reports for the tested code.

maintenance.text: Compiler and library versions affect validator APIs; the tutorial names dependencies explicitly.

costs.text: The compiler has Apache-2.0 terms; compiler licensing does not account for ledger transaction charges.

example.run_instructions: Place plldn.ak at lib/plldn.ak in the documented project layout. Create a project with aiken new, add lib/plldn.ak, and run aiken check. This tests only a pure decision function.
example.expected_result: accepts_minimum passes; no contract is deployed or transaction sent.

implementation.name: Alloy Analyzer
implementation.version_scope: Alloy Analyzer 6 family; introductory relational model, not temporal checking.

fit.text: Search relational designs for instances and counterexamples; bounded analysis applies to the specified search scope.

prerequisites.text: Learn sets, relations, quantifiers and constraints before reading generated model instances.

execution.text: Launch the Analyzer JAR with Java, open a model, and execute run or check.

behavior.text: Signatures describe sets and fields describe relations; facts constrain every explored instance.

tooling.text: The Analyzer bundles model finding, SAT solvers, libraries and examples; temporal tools can be additional dependencies.

maintenance.text: Adding a fact can exclude a counterexample an assertion was supposed to reveal.

costs.text: The root licence contains an applicability warning; no unambiguous whole-bundle SPDX expression is asserted.

example.run_instructions: Launch the Analyzer JAR with java -jar, open items.als and execute its run command.
example.expected_result: An instance contains at least one Item and a single Chosen atom related to exactly one Item.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: The root file says its Apache text is not yet valid and labels current code MIT. Audit the selected release and bundled solvers before redistribution.

implementation.name: AngelCode Scripting Library
implementation.version_scope: Embedded engine with documented C++ host registrations; not a standalone executable.

sources.label: AngelScript first script and host integration

fit.text: Embed typed scripts in C++ applications; the host chooses which native facilities scripts may access.

prerequisites.text: Understand C++ integration and registration before expecting scripts to perform host operations.

execution.text: A host creates the engine, builds a module and executes a function through a context.

behavior.text: String support and print are registered facilities; scripts cannot assume every embedding supplies them.

tooling.text: SDK add-ons and examples demonstrate integration; message callbacks explain errors alongside API return codes.

maintenance.text: Preserve the exposed native interface when changing the host; scripts depend on registered signatures.

costs.text: Commercial use is allowed subject to origin, modification and licence-notice restrictions.

example.run_instructions: Configure the first-script guide's host with the standard-string add-on and void print(const string &in). Build this script module and execute void main().
example.expected_result: The host print callback receives PLLDN; no standalone interpreter is assumed.
